Geoffrey Wall, of Barrie, Ontario, is alleged to have operated as an airline captain between 2009 and 2025 without a license to fly large commercial passenger planes, according to Peel regional police.

About 20,000 people have signed a petition on Change.org entitled Protect Japanese Manga, protesting against the official White House X account posting videos featuring unauthorised use of imagery from the popular Dragon Ball, Yu-Gi-Oh! and Naruto series.

euronews.title: Europe’s chaotic Entry/Exit System could take up to two years to stabilise, EU official warns
euronews.description: Two months after Europe’s new biometric border checks launched, long queues and inconsistent procedures continue to frustrate travellers. Now, a Frontex official has warned that the troubled Entry/Exit System could take up to two years to fully stabilise.

Au Liban, toujours régulièrement bombardé par l’armée israélienne, le chef de la diplomatie libanaise dit que les négociations directes avec Israël sont « la seule voie pour essayer de (…) régler le problème dans sa globalité ».

lemonde.description: Cette liste noire, qui devrait figurer dans le projet de loi sur la protection de l’enfance, empêchera toute forme de réemploi des personnes révoquées de l’éducation nationale en raison de leur comportement déplacé envers des mineurs, a détaillé Edouard Geffray.

lemonde.description: A l’issue de quarante-huit heures de garde à vue, le chanteur devait être présenté à trois juges d’instruction, mercredi, dans la journée.

lemonde.title: Gwynne Shotwell, vraie patronne de SpaceX et femme de confiance d’Elon Musk
lemonde.description: Entrée dans le groupe en 2002, la présidente et directrice générale opérationnelle a réussi à développer une entreprise qui écrase le marché mondial des lanceurs civils et militaires. A la veille de l’une des introductions en Bourse les plus ahurissantes de l’histoire, elle détient des actions de la firme valorisées à 1,7 milliard de dollars.

lemonde.description: Les cheminots font grève, mercredi, et demandent un moratoire sur l’ouverture à la concurrence ainsi que des hausses de salaire pour faire face à l’inflation.

lemonde.title: La Coupe du monde 2026, annoncée comme « la plus verte », pourrait devenir la plus polluante
lemonde.description: Alors que les pays hôtes annonçaient 3,6 millions de tonnes d’émissions de CO₂, les déplacements en avion des équipes et des supporteurs entre le Canada, les Etats-Unis et le Mexique pourraient faire exploser le bilan carbone de la compétition.

lemonde.title: En 2025, un chiffre d’affaires et un bénéfice stabilisés pour le Groupe Le Monde

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine | « Nous continuons d’appliquer les sanctions ukrainiennes » : Volodymyr Zelensky salue les attaques contre des sites pétroliers et militaires en Russie
lemonde.description: Le président ukrainien a notamment cité le bombardement, dans la nuit de mardi à mercredi, d’une usine militaire à Tcheboksary et l’attaque sur une raffinerie de pétrole, dans la région de Samara, à plus de 900 kilomètres du front.

lemonde.title: Dans « Le Vertige », Quentin Dupieux revigore son univers absurde et loufoque en animation
lemonde.description: Réalisé avec de jeunes diplômés de l’Ecole des Gobelins, le nouveau film du prolifique cinéaste, à l’esthétique volontairement artisanale, met en scène des personnages dérivés d’acteurs réels, Jonathan Cohen, Alain Chabat et Anaïs Demoustier.

france24fr.title: RD Congo : des migrants sud-américains expulsés des États-Unis vers Kinshasa renvoyés chez eux
france24fr.description: La plupart des migrants sud-américains expulsés des États-Unis vers Kinshasa, en République démocratique du Congo, ont finalement été renvoyés dans leur pays d’origine. Arrivés mi-avril dans le cadre d’un dispositif américain controversé d’expulsion vers des pays tiers, ils ne sont donc pas restés en RDC.

france24fr.title: Ebola : violent bras de fer au Kenya à propos d'un site de quarantaine américain
france24fr.description: Au Kenya, un centre de quarantaine destiné aux ressortissants américains touchés par Ebola crée la polémique. Sa construction suscite la peur des habitants, qui ont manifesté face à la police. Récit de Julien Dubois.

france24fr.title: En images : la Sagrada Familia, un joyau architectural qui accueille le pape Léon XIV
france24fr.description: À l'occasion du centenaire de la mort de l'architecte Antoni Gaudi, le pape Léon XIV doit bénir mercredi la plus grande tour de la basilique de la Sagrada Familia à Barcelone, puis célébrer une messe dans ce qui est aujourd'hui la plus haute église du monde. L'édifice, dont la construction a débuté en 1882 et est toujours inachevée, attire tous les ans des millions de visiteurs.

france24fr.title: Belfast: violences anti-immigrés après une attaque au couteau
france24fr.description: Des violences anti-immigrés ont éclaté dans la ville de #Belfast, en Irlande du Nord, après l'arrestation d'un #réfugié soudanais soupçonné de tentative de #meurtre. La vidéo de l'agression au couteau avait été largement relayée sur les réseaux sociaux, notamment par l'extrême droite.

france24fr.title: L'arbitre somalien refoulé des États-Unis accueilli par la foule à Mogadiscio
france24fr.description: 🇸🇴⚽ L’arbitre somalien Omar Artan, sacré meilleur arbitre africain l’an dernier, a été refoulé samedi à son arrivée aux États-Unis. La FIFA a finalement annoncé qu’il ne dirigera aucun match lors de la Coupe du monde de football. En Somalie, la décision a provoqué une vive indignation, et à son retour à Mogadiscio, il a été accueilli par une foule.

france24fr.title: Le savika : un sport malgache ou les hommes se mesurent aux zébus
france24fr.description: Si la corrida espagnole est connue dans le monde entier, peu de gens savent qu'une tradition similaire existe depuis plusieurs siècles à Madagascar : le savika. Comme dans la corrida, l'homme défie l'animal dans une arène. Mais ici, pas de mise à mort : le but est de s'accrocher le plus longtemps possible sur le dos d'un zébu lâché dans l'arène. Une discipline transmise de génération en génération, que Madagascar aimerait voir inscrite au patrimoine culturel immatériel de l'Unesco. Reportage de

france24fr.title: Le Sénégal veut rassurer ses partenaires avant le rendez-vous avec le FMI
france24fr.description: À quelques jours d’une visite importante du FMI au Sénégal, Dakar envoie un signal positif à ses partenaires internationaux. Le Sénégal a procédé au paiement anticipé de deux échéances de sa dette. L’objectif du nouveau gouvernement est de trouver un accord avec l’institution et de relancer l’économie, qui souffre depuis 18 mois. Précisions du correspondant de France 24 à Dakar, Elimane Ndao.

france24fr.title: Que sont devenus les migrants sud-américains expulsés par les États-Unis en RD Congo ?
france24fr.description: Que sont devenus les migrants sud-américains expulsés des États-Unis vers la RD Congo ? Ils étaient arrivés mi-avril dans le cadre d’un dispositif américain controversé d’expulsion de ressortissants étrangers en situation irrégulière vers des pays tiers. La plupart d’entre eux ont été renvoyés dans leur pays d’origine, précisions d’Aurélie Bazzara-Kibangula, correspondante de France 24 à Kinshasa.

france24fr.title: Philippines : les secouristes poursuivent leurs efforts après un séisme meurtrier
france24fr.description: Des blessés soignés dehors en pleine chaleur, des secours ralentis par les répliques et des accès coupés : au lendemain du puissant séisme qui a frappé le sud des Philippines faisant au moins 41 morts, des milliers de personnes sont toujours déplacées mardi. La secousse de magnitude 7,8 qui s'est produite lundi au large des côtes de Mindanao a provoqué l'effondrement de bâtiments et déclenché des glissements de terrain dans une grande partie de l'île. Récit de Marc Paupe.

france24fr.title: La Patrouile de France survole la statue de la Liberté à New York
france24fr.description: Un survol à haute valeur symbolique. La patrouille de France a fait son show dans le ciel de New York, suivie de son traditionnel panache bleu blanc et rouge. La formation d'élite de l'aviation française a survolé la Statue de la Liberté, un cadeau de la France aux États-Unis, qui célèbrent les 250 ans de leur indépendance.

france24fr.title: Reprise des frappes américaines en Iran : seule option de Donald Trump ?
france24fr.description: Nouvelle escalade ces dernières heures au Moyen Orient. L'Iran a frappé la Jordanie, le Bahreïn et le Koweït… pays du Golfe accusés de porter la responsabilité morale des frappes américaines sur le sol iranien. Washington présente ces bombardements comme des représailles après qu'un de ses hélicoptères a été abattu par la République islamique. Donald Trump avait-il d’autres choix ? Analyse d’Axel May, chroniqueur international France 24.

france24fr.title: 52 ans plus tard, Haïti de retour à la Coupe du Monde de football
france24fr.description: La Coupe du Monde 2026 commencera demain et une équipe va faire son retour dans la compétition après 52 ans d’absence… celle d’Haïti. L’équipe est entraînée par un français et aucun de ses joueurs ne joue dans le pays. Récit de Victor Faubert.

france24fr.title: Des frappes pakistanaises sur l'Afghanistan font plusieurs morts
france24fr.description: Le Pakistan a affirmé mercredi avoir tué 26 personnes liées aux Taliban pakistanais, dans des frappes aériennes qualifiées de "précises et calibrées" à la frontière avec l'Afghanistan, après que Kaboul a déclaré que 12 personnes, dont des enfants, sont mortes dans l'attaque.

france24fr.title: "Je suis un prisonnier d'opinion" : à Bakou, l'opposant Karimli jugé pour "tentative de coup d'État"
france24fr.description: Ali Karimli, chef du Parti du front populaire d’Azerbaïdjan et figure centrale de l’opposition dans ce pays depuis plus de 30 ans, est jugé mercredi à Bakou pour "tentative de coup d’État". Depuis sa prison, celui que l'on compare souvent à Alexeï Navalny a accepté de répondre aux questions de France 24. Il dénonce des accusations "fabriquées de toutes pièces” par le président Aliev et évoque le risque d’un assassinat politique.

france24fr.title: Sagrada Familia : génie ou folie ? Parlons-en avec Marc Jampolsky et Béatrice Bizot
france24fr.description: C'est le jour J à Barcelone. Le pape Léon XIV doit inaugurer et bénir, mercredi 10 juin, la tour de Jésus, la plus haute tour de la Sagrada Família, la cathédrale imaginée par Antoni Gaudi. La fin des travaux de cette tour emblématique marque une étape importante pour un chantier qui dure depuis plus de 140 ans. Parlons-en avec Marc Jampolsky, réalisateur de "Sagrada Família, le rêve achevé de Gaudi" (Arte), et Béatrice Bizot, sculptrice.

france24fr.title: Des frappes israéliennes tuent au moins 11 personnes à Tyr, ville côtière du Liban
france24fr.description: Au moins onze personnes ont été tuées dans la ville de Tyr au Liban, après une frappe d'Israël sur cette ville portuaire relativement épargnée jusque-là. Plus tôt, l'État hébreu avait lancé un appel à l'évacuation à l'ensemble des habitants de la ville. Des files de voitures se sont formées et de nombreux habitants ont fui leurs habitations de peur d'être visés par les frappes. Récit de Jean Barrère.

france24fr.title: Libye : Derna renaît de ses cendres après le cyclone Daniel
france24fr.description: En Libye, le cyclone Daniel a frappé de plein fouet la ville de Derna il y a trois ans, faisant des milliers de victimes. Cette catastrophe a mis en lumière de graves failles de sécurité, notamment la rupture de barrages vétustes datant des années 1970. Aujourd'hui, malgré le traumatisme profond des habitants, les chantiers de reconstruction sont déjà bien avancés.

observador.title: BCE deve subir juros como "tiro de aviso" contra a inflação
observador.description: Primeira subida de juros em três anos deverá ser de 25 pontos-base. Intenção é sinalizar que BCE não irá tolerar que se forme uma escalada súbita da inflação, como aconteceu em 2022.

observador.title: Surto de ébola causa 115 mortos na RD Congo

observador.description: Nove homens e três mulheres foram mortos no subúrbio de Cleveland e nove pessoas ficaram feridas no ataque a tiro. Grupo de mais de 10 agressores ainda não foi localizado pela polícia.

observador.title: Homem morto a tiro a um quilómetro de percurso do Papa
observador.description: Vítima de cerca de 40 anos foi atingida na cabeça e morreu no local, perto do percurso por onde Papa vai passar. É o segundo assassinato em Barcelona numa semana.

observador.title: 16 concertos a não perder no Primavera Sound
observador.description: O festival arranca esta quinta-feira, 11 de junho, e prolonga-se até domingo. Gorillaz, Amaarae, Massive Attack, The xx, Sudan Archives ou Bad Gyal entre os principais destaques. Eis um roteiro.

observador.title: À procura de um Canal que possa evitar as vitórias morais
observador.description: Panamá chegou pela segunda vez a uma fase final do Mundial e quer mostrar evolução nos últimos anos para evitar as três derrotas de 2018. As carências existem, a vontade de ultrapassá-las também.

observador.title: Queiroz, uma lição de Mandela e as aulas de Semenyo
observador.description: Gana despediu Otto Addo a pouco mais de dois meses do Mundial e apostou em Carlos Queiroz para ter resultados imediatos. Africanos não passam fase de grupos desde 2010 – mas têm agora novas "armas".

observador.title: "Rússia e China são os "adultos na sala" a salvar Trump"

observador.title: A Last Dance de um pequeno Super Herói de máscara
observador.description: Nunca aparece no topo das apostas, vai sempre parar ao topo das apostas. A Croácia é aquela seleção que gosta de vestir o fato de outsider porque entra sempre na festa. Neste caso, a última de Modric.

observador.title: "Olá, tio!" Menor usa código em alerta à PSP de abuso sexual
observador.description: Menor realizou chamada de emergência de 14 minutos na presença do abusador. Informação comunicada à polícia permitiu intercetar carro onde seguiam. Agente recebeu louvor da Direção Nacional da PSP.

observador.title: A missão de endireitar aquilo que começou a nascer torto
observador.description: Depois dos sinais de alarme nos particulares de março, ausência de alguns "pesos pesados" aumentou pressão sobre Tuchel. Sem olhar a nomes, o técnico tem uma gasolina chamada convicção. E Kane, claro.

observador.title: Olá, Marco! Adiós, Mourinho — SLB termina “série de netflix”
observador.description: Comunicado de Mourinho termina uma novela longa e na qual Rui Costa deve explicações. Marco Silva vai ter autonomia suficiente ao comando? Ainda o último teste da seleção nacional antes do Mundial.

observador.title: Mourinho despede-se e agradece "honra" de treinar Benfica
observador.description: Da presidência ao staff do Benfica Campus, Mourinho não esqueceu ninguém na estrutura dos encarnados na hora da despedida. Agradeceu a Rui Costa e garantiu que jogadores serão seus "para sempre".

observador.title: Miqui Otero: "A nostalgia é a gentrificação da memória"
observador.description: Em "Orquestra", é a música que narra os acontecimentos em noite de festa popular numa aldeia galega. A partir desse microcosmo, é explorado o passado e presente de Espanha. Falámos com o seu autor.

observador.title: Coreia do Sul alerta para acordo entre Pequim e Pyongyang
observador.description: Seul alertou que proposta de Xi Jinping para ampliar intercâmbios militares com a Coreia do Norte não tem precedentes. Presidente chinês visitou Pyongyang e defendeu mais cooperação com Pyongyang.

observador.title: Seguro quer "relação de equilíbrio" com aliados
observador.description: No seu primeiro discurso do 10 de junho, Presidente defendeu "cooperação com aliados", mas destacou que Portugal tem "liberdade de decisão e responsabilidade”.

spiegel.title: Steffen Krach: SPD-Bürgermeisterkandidat in Berlin zweifelt an großem Reformpaket der Bundesregierung vor Sommer
spiegel.description: Berlins SPD-Chef Steffen Krach glaubt nicht mehr an ein großes Reformpaket vor dem Sommer. Die Koalition verbreite Angst, sagt der Bürgermeisterkandidat – und lädt den Kanzler ein, sich die Wut am Wahlkampfstand anzuhören.

spiegel.title: Infrastrukturzukunftsgesetz: SPD kontert Merz-Kritik an angeblicher Gesetzesblockade
spiegel.description: Kanzler Merz hat in einer Fraktionssitzung kritisiert, dass sich der Koalitionspartner beim Infrastrukturzukunftsgesetz querstelle. Die SPD zeigt sich überrascht – und erinnert an den Zeitplan.

spiegel.description: Über Nina Warkens Sparpaket soll im Bundestag beraten werden. Die Gesundheitsministerin steht von mehreren Seiten unter Druck. Dem früheren Präsidenten des Bundessozialgerichts geht die Reform nicht weit genug.

spiegel.title: Jeffrey Epstein Files: Die Suche nach der verschwundenen Michele aus Deutschland
spiegel.description: 2015 verlässt sie mit Koffer und Pass die Wohnung, seitdem wurde Michele nie wieder gesehen. So haben der SPIEGEL und das ZDF versucht, die Geschichte der jungen Frau zu rekonstruieren.

spiegel.title: Vermisste Deutsche: Die wichtigsten Fragen und Antworten zum Fall Michele

spiegel.title: RTL-Managerin Inga Leschek: Wie der »King of GerMMAny« zum Risiko wird

new-sci.description: Physics is considered a cold, hard science – but it will transform your life if you view it with a bit more subjectivity, says Karmela Padavic-Callaghan

new-sci.description: Brown dwarfs are somewhere between the size of a planet and a star, so how could we have potentially mistaken two of them for distant galaxies? Columnist Chanda Prescod-Weinstein argues that solving this cosmic mix-up is particularly possible now, as galaxy research has never been stronger

new-sci.title: Dinosaur-killing asteroid impact site stayed hot for millions of years
new-sci.description: Drill cores at the impact site of the Chicxulub asteroid show evidence that, alongside widespread destruction, the collision created a vast underground ecosystem filled with hot water that sheltered microbial life

new-sci.title: Unpicking endometriosis reveals how it affects more than the pelvis
new-sci.description: Endometriosis is usually thought of as a gynaecological condition, but a huge study shows it has links with cholesterol levels, inflammation and an altered microbiome

new-sci.title: What really happened when ancient humans migrated out of Africa
new-sci.description: The out-of-Africa migration, in which ancient humans went on to inhabit every other continent except Antarctica, may not have been one moment in time, but a long and slow process. Columnist Michael Marshall examines how archaeologists are rethinking this critical part of our history

new-sci.title: What is a ‘normal’ memory slowdown, and when should I worry?
new-sci.description: Lapses in memory are a normal part of ageing but can also be signs of dementia. Here’s how to distinguish between typical brain ageing and cognitive decline

new-sci.title: Wildlife thrives in solar farm built on restored peatland
new-sci.description: A diverse range of bird species has been recorded at a solar park on rewetted peatland in Germany, suggesting that combining energy generation with habitat restoration could benefit biodiversity, the climate and the economy

new-sci.title: Can Apple and Google stop children from sharing explicit images?
new-sci.description: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer has warned tech firms, including Apple and Google, that they must voluntarily implement tools to stop children sharing explicit images, but experts warn this is easier said than done

new-sci.description: Mice seemed to reap some of the benefits of sleep by having their brain activity stimulated while they were awake, and the researchers plan to test the approach on people

new-sci.description: A team in the US has reported promising results after using an improved form of CRISPR to gene-edit human embryos, but a major issue remains unsolved

phys-org.description: There are encouraging signs for the endangered Maugean skate, with a new monitoring report finding that a new cohort of skates born in Macquarie Harbor has reached adulthood.

phys-org.title: War on drugs or war on the poor? How bandit hunting formed a cover for Mexico's counterinsurgency campaign
phys-org.description: If the drug trade has helped define the modern Mexican state, writes the author of a new article in The Social History of Alcohol and Drugs, so too have wars on drugs. In "From Bandit Hunting to a War Against 'Social Poisoners': Counterinsurgency as Drug War and Drug War as Counterinsurgency in 1960s–1970s Southern Mexico," author Alexander Aviña argues that the strategies eventually employed against Mexican drug traders were first developed in the violent suppression of rural guerrill

phys-org.title: Majorana modes withstand disorder in atomic chains, boosting fault-tolerant quantum computing
phys-org.description: Quantum computers—systems that process information and perform computations by leveraging the principles of quantum mechanics—could solve some tasks faster and more effectively than classical computers. While some studies have demonstrated the advantages of these computers for specific tasks, ensuring their reliable operation in real-world settings has proved challenging.

phys-org.title: How cultural backgrounds shape financial forecasts
phys-org.description: There's a funny thing about facts. Two people can look at the same ones but interpret them very differently, depending on their styles of thinking. On Wall Street, analysts with short-term or long-term orientations may issue different financial forecasts for the same company, says Yong Yu, professor of accounting at the McCombs School of Business at The University of Texas at Austin.

phys-org.title: Quantum witness technique reveals spinons in quantum spin liquid candidate
phys-org.description: Physicists at University College Cork have developed a new approach in the search for a quantum spin liquid, a long-sought state of quantum matter resembling a magnetic liquid whose quantum properties mean it never freezes. The work is a key step in the search for quantum silicon, a mineral that could be used to create quantum computers, just as silicon is used in traditional computers. The resulting paper appears in Nature Physics.

phys-org.title: People have an inherent preference for counterclockwise motion, study reveals
phys-org.description: Researchers in Spain and Japan tested a broad range of pedestrians in varying group sizes to see whether there were any patterns in their turning behaviors, and what factors influenced them, if any. It turns out that the vast majority of people prefer counterclockwise turning. Most factors, such as culture or gender, made little difference. Only age showed a noticeable but small change, in that younger people followed this pattern more strongly.

phys-org.title: Why plastic lingers: Water chemistry slows nature's cleanup
phys-org.description: Scientists have long known that sunlight helps break down plastic. So, why do plastic products linger for decades and even centuries in rivers, lakes, and oceans—even when bathed in direct sunlight? Northwestern University engineers have uncovered an unexpected answer. The surprising culprit is the water itself.

phys-org.title: Stretchy, soft, and sticky: Advancing the next generation of wearable and implantable sensors
phys-org.description: Wearable and implantable biosensors have the potential to revolutionize health care by diagnosing, monitoring, and even treating a wide range of health conditions. Recent innovations in the lab of Wei Gao, professor of medical engineering at Caltech and a Heritage Medical Research Institute Investigator, are pushing the field forward through the creation of soft, stretchable, tissue-integrated bioelectronics for continuous sensing and adaptive therapy.

phys-org.title: JWST reveals dawn-dusk atmosphere split on ultra-hot exoplanet WASP-121 b
phys-org.description: Astronomers have revealed distinct differences in atmospheric conditions between the morning and evening transition zones of the ultra-hot gas planet WASP-121 b, which separate day from night, commonly called terminators. This achievement was only possible due to the unmatched sensitivity of the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST).

phys-org.title: Italian astronaut to pilot Artemis III mission
phys-org.description: Italian astronaut Luca Parmitano is hoping to bring a taste of his homeland to the Artemis III mission, which he will pilot near Earth in 2027 to test two lunar modules.

phys-org.title: To discover new physics, AI may need to 'unlearn' the old one
phys-org.description: A study in the Journal of Cosmology and Astroparticle Physics explores how a machine-learning strategy known as transfer learning could dramatically reduce the computational cost of searching for new physics beyond the standard cosmological model—while also revealing an unexpected risk: Sometimes AI systems can become too reliant on what they already know.

phys-org.title: Study finds fishing bycatch does not attract lesser black-backed gulls out of wind farms
phys-org.description: Lesser black-backed gulls from the colony on the Dutch island of Neeltje Jans appear to avoid the wind farm off the Zeeland coast, with the exception of some males. NIOZ ecologist Rosemarie Kentie and her colleagues suspected the gulls were attracted by fishing boats outside the wind farm and the bycatch thrown overboard. This turned out not to be the case: Even during weekends, when there is little fishing, the birds rarely visit the wind farm.

phys-org.title: Theoretical model developed to understand how isotopes change spectroscopy results
phys-org.description: When researchers want to uncover what atoms make up a material, they turn to a number of tried-and-true spectroscopy methods. Spectroscopy works by shining a specific type of light onto a substance and then analyzing how that light is either absorbed, emitted, or scattered. Every atom has a different way of interacting with light, and scientists study this light-matter interaction to identify the atoms in the material.

phys-org.title: Survival of five million amphibians and reptiles displaced by construction in British Columbia may not be tracked
phys-org.description: UBC researchers have found that more than five million amphibians and reptiles were displaced by development in British Columbia in just four years—and that there is no requirement to monitor survival rates. The paper published in the Journal of Wildlife Management is the first of its kind to document the large-scale herpetofauna relocation taking place in the province.

phys-org.title: How health care systems shape native preferences for immigrants
phys-org.description: In recent years, anti-immigration sentiment has become increasingly common around the world. A common concern surrounding immigration is its potential impact on the host country's welfare system, including health care. Such concerns can reduce public support for accepting immigrants and for redistributive welfare policies.

phys-org.title: Strong leadership will be key as AI reshapes the workforce, argues research
phys-org.description: As artificial intelligence changes how work gets done, experts say strong leadership will play a critical role in helping employees adapt to shifting responsibilities, evolving technologies and changing workplace demands. The findings are published in the journal Human Resource Development Review.

phys-org.title: Physicists harness potential of quantum phase transitions
phys-org.description: Researchers at University College Dublin and international collaborators have just published a detailed and accessible guide that aims to translate theoretical ideas into practical devices for quantum enhanced sensing technologies.

phys-org.title: Satellite data reveal hidden labor trafficking in Brazil
phys-org.description: A Stanford team used geospatial data and detection algorithms to achieve a tenfold increase in rescues from modern slavery in the Brazilian Amazon. Now, they are planning to expand their approach.

undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

undark.title: Book Review:  The Case for Making Data-Driven Decisions
undark.description: In “Beyond Belief: How Evidence Shows What Really Works,” science journalist Helen Pearson profiles a group of people working in medicine and other fields who became leaders of the worldwide evidence movement, which encourages the use of data from rigorous research to direct treatments, policies, and plans.

undark.title: What the Hantavirus Story Reveals About Medical Mistrust
undark.description: The reaction to an outbreak of hantavirus on a cruise ship reveals a story about mistrust in medicine and public health. In the U.S., hantavirus disproportionately kills Native Americans. A doctor who works at a hospital on Navajo Nation writes that such mistrust always lands hardest on the most vulnerable.

undark.title: Book Review: The Mind-Boggling Science of Enormous Numbers
undark.description: In “Huge Numbers: A Story of Counting Ambitiously, From 4½ to Fish 7,” mathematician Richard Elwes shows off his love of all things numeric, and, in particular, shines a spotlight on some of the largest numbers humans have ever contemplated, and the much larger numbers that await those who seek them out.

undark.title: When Scientific Arguments Obscure Moral Ones, Democracy Suffers
undark.description: The Pentagon’s new vaccine policy values individual choice over public health. Which of these values should be prioritized is a legitimate subject for democratic debate. But when experts respond to moral arguments animating policy decisions by reiterating facts, it undermines debate and fuels divisiveness.

This indicates China’s progress on financial deepening and underscores markets' increasingly central role in shaping the economy.

proj-syn.title: The Future of Development Finance Is Not Primarily About Money
proj-syn.description: Multilateral development banks have not kept pace with changes to the global financial environment. For middle-income countries like India, accessing knowledge and technology is now a bigger challenge than raising capital, which suggests that these institutions must rethink their operating model.

proj-syn.title: Nigeria’s Perilous French Gambit
proj-syn.description: Nigeria’s increasingly close relationship with France marks a departure from six decades of foreign policy aimed at reducing French influence in West Africa. An increasingly close relationship with a power that has long sought to undermine Nigerian influence in West Africa will benefit only politically connected business elites.

proj-syn.title: Autocracy Is Fueling Mexico’s Fiscal Deterioration
proj-syn.description: Mexico’s recent ratings downgrades are merely a symptom of a more serious malady: the ruling Morena party’s efforts to consolidate power permanently. To ensure the legal predictability foreign investors require, President Claudia Sheinbaum would need to confront Morena’s ideological legacy and, more importantly, its cartel ties.

proj-syn.title: The Trump Economy Is Bad News for Republicans
proj-syn.description: Donald Trump triumphed in the 2024 election by continually hammering on the Biden administration’s dismal inflation record. If his party gets shellacked in this year’s midterm elections, it will be because he has made Americans even worse off.

proj-syn.title: SpaceX Is the New East India Company
proj-syn.description: Although SpaceX is not about to rule over foreign subjects, as the chartered companies founded in the early modern era did, it, too, is operating beyond the reach of any sovereign. And like its predecessors, it has already accumulated immense powers that governments will struggle to reclaim.

proj-syn.title: The ECB Should Not Raise Interest Rates Yet
proj-syn.description: Against a backdrop of acute uncertainty, weak growth, subdued wages, and elevated market interest rates, monetary tightening is warranted only when there is convincing evidence that higher inflation is becoming entrenched. No such evidence has yet materialized in Europe.

proj-syn.title: When Markets Run on Empty
proj-syn.description: Markets are flying high despite geopolitical turmoil because a broad-based willingness to keep spending has been matched by an ability to keep doing so. But as more economic participants exhaust their means and rely on debt, a painful moment of truth will arrive—sooner rather than later if the Strait of Hormuz remains closed.

proj-syn.title: The Pope and the AI Profiteers
proj-syn.description: In his first encyclical, Pope Leo XIV rightly rejects the idea that markets alone can be trusted to shape society’s technological future. Recognizing that AI raises questions that prices and profits cannot answer, the Chicago-born pope has posed a direct challenge to Chicago School economics.

proj-syn.title: AI Must Not Encroach on Human Dignity
proj-syn.description: In a world captivated by technological advances, Pope Leo XIV’s first encyclical seeks to shift attention away from the marvels and terrors of AI and toward the magnificence of humanity. The message that the technology lacks a “moral conscience” and is distinct from human cognition is necessary and welcome.

proj-syn.title: The Key Forces Now Shaping Markets and Geopolitics
proj-syn.description: Three major factors are likely to shape economic and geopolitical outcomes over the next several years: politically unconstrained AI development, a shift from the logic of globalization to zero-sum thinking, and heightened international tail risks. Much could go right, or at least as expected—until it doesn’t.

proj-syn.title: The Living Ghosts of Violent Radicalism
proj-syn.description: Following World War II, the most militant student movements emerged in the former Axis powers as a way to cope with previous generations' complicity. But while the Red Army Faction and others were haunted by memories of past crimes, today's young people have mostly forgotten, and a growing number think far-right politics are cool.

proj-syn.title: Using AI to Test Policy Language
proj-syn.description: Policymakers have long understood that language affects economic behavior, but until recently, there were few tools capable of systematically analyzing its effects. AI may now help close that gap, enabling officials to anticipate how framing and timing can move markets and shift public opinion.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Competitiveness Bogeyman
proj-syn.description: Calls for European leaders to protect domestic industry from "unfairly" subsidized Chinese competition have lately grown louder. But while tariffs might offer temporary relief to a few sectors, they cannot restore Europe's technological leadership, industrial dynamism, or export competitiveness.
